query: How does resolution time vary across category, priority, and assignment group?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: A finer-grained categorisation derived from short_description gives a new axis to group resolution time beyond the coarse original category column. Values (vpn, database, email, network_connectivity) are sound readings of the source descriptions.

per_column.name: affected_system
per_column.rationale: Maps descriptions to specific systems (vpn_gateway, email_server, wifi), providing a useful grouping dimension. Values are well-warranted inferences from the text, though somewhat correlated with incident_category.

per_column.name: failure_symptom
per_column.rationale: Symptom type (connection_failure, outage_down, access_denied) is a distinct analytical axis that could correlate with resolution time. Mostly grounded, though 'Email system not working properly' -> 'outage_down' is a mild over-specification of a vague description.

per_column.name: scope_qualifier
per_column.rationale: Scope (remote_access, department_specific, location_specific) is a plausible new grouping dimension relevant to resolution time. Values like 'department_specific' for WiFi in sales are well grounded; 'general' as default for silent rows is acceptable.

per_column.name: resolver_match
per_column.rationale: Presumably whether assigned_to matches closed_by; a plausible axis but the boolean is coarse. Row evidence samples do not expose assigned_to/closed_by, and same-timestamp VPN row labelled True vs others False is not verifiable from provided text, so groundedness is uncertain.

per_column.name: assignment_lag_present
per_column.rationale: Near-constant (428 true / 72 false) giving little discriminative leverage. Derivation from timestamps is plausible but not verifiable in the samples, where every row is labelled True; low grounding support.

per_column.name: caller_id_group
per_column.rationale: This is essentially a copy of the existing caller_id values (Don Goodliffe, Bud Richman, etc.), trivially redundant with an original column and not an axis the query (category/priority/assignment_group) calls for. Grounded but adds no leverage.

per_column.name: resolution_delay_proxy
per_column.rationale: Directly bins resolution time, which is the core dependent variable of the query -- highly useful. However samples show closed_at == sys_updated_on with no opened_at, and the VPN row is 'same_day' while identical-timestamp rows are 'one_to_three_days', suggesting the underlying duration computation is only partially verifiable/consistent.

judge.rationale: The text-derived categorisation columns (incident_category, affected_system, failure_symptom, scope_qualifier) provide genuine new grouping axes well aligned with the query and are soundly grounded in the short_description text. resolution_delay_proxy is the most useful column as it bins the target variable, though its exact derivation is only partially verifiable and shows minor inconsistency across identical-timestamp rows. caller_id_group is a trivial restatement of an existing column and adds no leverage for this query. resolver_match and assignment_lag_present are weaker: near-constant and/or not verifiable from the provided evidence samples. Overall the set leans useful and mostly grounded with a few weak members.
